HOME HEALTH SKILLED NURSING / SPEECH THERAPY VISIT NOTE

Patient: 78-year-old male with history of ischemic stroke (right MCA distribution, 3 months ago) resulting in moderate oropharyngeal dysphagia, confirmed by modified barium swallow study showing delayed pharyngeal transit and mild aspiration with thin liquids.

Physician oversight: Patient remains under the care of his attending neurologist, Dr. R. Alvarez, who continues to monitor his post-stroke recovery and swallowing status via monthly office and home health visits.

Homebound status: Patient requires maximal assistance and a wheelchair for any ambulation outside the home due to residual left hemiparesis and poor endurance. He is unable to leave home without considerable and taxing effort, and does so only for medical appointments. This has been documented in the home health intake assessment and subsequent visit notes.

Plan of care: A home health plan of care was established, signed and dated by Dr. Alvarez on 09/02, outlining skilled speech therapy services including swallow rehabilitation exercises and surface electrical stimulation (NMES) to the anterior neck musculature to improve pharyngeal swallow function, three times weekly for four weeks.

Face-to-face encounter: Dr. Alvarez saw the patient in the office on 08/20, ten days prior to the start of home health services on 08/30, and documented the ongoing dysphagia, aspiration risk, and need for skilled therapy services in the clinical record.

Skilled need: The speech-language pathologist is providing skilled, medically necessary treatment for the patient's dysphagia given his aspiration risk, inability to safely progress diet without therapeutic intervention, and need for professional judgment in adjusting the electrical stimulation parameters and swallow exercise regimen based on his evolving neurological status. Today's session included electrode placement over the suprahyoid muscle group, stimulation at 20 Hz for effortful swallow facilitation, and caregiver education on aspiration precautions. Patient tolerated treatment well with no adverse effects noted.

Recertification: Given the anticipated need for ongoing skilled dysphagia therapy beyond the initial 60-day episode, recertification will be scheduled and coordinated with the certifying physician prior to the end of the current episode.

Plan: Continue skilled SLP visits per plan of care; reassess swallow function in 2 weeks with repeat clinical bedside evaluation.
